purpose.summary: Add a bounded passive mainnet-prefix smoke that transfers the first 288 blocks from the exact legacy baseline to a fresh candidate over loopback and compares independently restarted chain-state observations.
scope: Let the exact baseline obtain the public mainnet prefix through height 288 without authored transactions, blocks, wallet activity, inbound public service, or assumed-valid shortcuts.
Restart the baseline offline, expose it only on loopback, synchronize a fresh candidate exclusively from that baseline, then restart the candidate offline.
Override minimum-chain-work and tip-age IBD service gates only on the already validated loopback baseline server so it can serve the bounded historical prefix.
Compare genesis and the height-288 block hash, raw header, and chainwork while binding distinct binaries, processes, ports, datadirs, and closed child environments.
Emit only a sanitized tri-state report after every process and temporary datadir has been removed.
exclusions: No production-node, consensus, validation, build, wallet, Chronik, activation, testnet, mainnet-parameter, cockpit-state, workflow, or roadmap change.
No transaction or block creation, mining, fee-market behavior, mempool comparison, DAA transition, reorganization, current-tip synchronization, full-history replay, or sustained-operation claim.
No raw child output, peer address, absolute host path, parent environment, cookie, secret, port, datadir, or runtime artifact enters the report.
No successful local run may be called reproduced evidence before separate public reconstruction and independent validation.

files.test_reachability: Runs the bounded passive mainnet-prefix legacy-to-candidate bridge, compares immutable checkpoint 288, and emits its sanitized tri-state report.
Exercises the runner lifecycle, bounded scope, network closure, privacy contract, cleanup, and contradiction/inconclusive classifications without contacting a network.

commands: Build exact Bitcoin Static v24.0.5 commit 2e8d5f7635c899cc99e71f06dedbe72b3ff7f07b in a clean dedicated build root.
expected_results: The clean baseline source and executable identities are recorded externally and remain unchanged through the scenario.

commands: Build the exact direct-child ERGON-CHANGE-0016 candidate in a distinct clean build root with the same build profile.
expected_results: The clean candidate source and executable identities are recorded externally and remain unchanged through the scenario.

scenarios.command: Run tests/compatibility/mainnet/run_passive_smoke.py with the exact baseline and candidate executables, a new work root, and a new report path.
expected_results: The baseline acquires mainnet blocks through checkpoint 288, the candidate acquires the same prefix only from the loopback baseline, both restart offline, their checkpoint observations match, and cleanup completes.
failure_conditions: Any binary, datadir, port, process, network-surface, chain, checkpoint, restart, resource-bound, report-privacy, or cleanup violation fails closed; unavailable or incomplete network acquisition remains inconclusive.

platforms: Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 public reproduction after technical acceptance

limitations: A successful 288-block run would establish only one bounded historical-prefix observation and one legacy-to-candidate loopback transfer path.
The stop trigger may complete already in-flight blocks above height 288; the report compares only immutable checkpoint 288 and rejects an exit height above the declared bound.

The loopback baseline server uses minimumchainwork=0 and a wide maxtipage only after the public prefix has been acquired and independently restarted; those settings affect historical serving availability, not block validation or the public fetch.

The prefix does not reach the current tip and does not establish full historical replay, sustained public peering, operator-binary parity, mining, mempool, DAA, reorganization, pruning, Chronik, activation, or mainnet readiness.
The baseline public peers and DNS resolvers necessarily observe the baseline source IP, while the candidate has no public peer and accepts no public inbound connection.
The harness binds executable bytes but relies on an external reviewed build record to bind each executable to its exact source.
The stage remains legacy-compatibility because mainnet-compatible deployment is a promotion of unchanged legacy behavior, not a post-testnet activation stage.
counterevidence: No public reconstruction of this profile exists at record-review time, so mainnet-prefix agreement for the exact candidate remains an Open Question.

A local macOS run matched checkpoint 288 using distinct-inode copies of the same exact legacy executable; it validates the harness topology but does not establish a candidate source-to-binary build binding.
The reproduced synthetic regtest matrix in ERGON-CHANGE-0015 does not answer public-network discovery, mainnet-prefix acquisition, or baseline-to-candidate mainnet P2P transfer.
